name: Nahum Tate and Nicholas Brady
bio: Nahum Tate (1652–1715), born in Dublin, settled in London, where he wrote plays, adapted Shakespeare's King Lear with a happy ending (the version that held the stage for over a century), supplied the libretto for Purcell's Dido and Aeneas, and in 1692 succeeded Thomas Shadwell as Poet Laureate. Nicholas Brady (1659–1726), also Irish-born, was a clergyman who served as chaplain to William III and Mary II.

Together they produced A New Version of the Psalms of David, first published in 1696 as a modern replacement for the old Sternhold and Hopkins psalter. Sung in the Church of England for well over a century, it gave the hymn-book such pieces as 'As pants the hart for cooling streams' (Psalm 42) and 'Through all the changing scenes of life' (Psalm 34); a Supplement of hymns followed a few years later.
